module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 9

References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.9)
- [BlSi20] Bloom, Thomas F., and Olof Sisask. "Breaking the logarithmic barrier in Roth's theorem on
  arithmetic progressions." arXiv preprint arXiv:2007.03528 (2020).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Green9

/--
The quantity $r_k(N)$, defined as the size of the largest subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ without
non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progressions.
-/
noncomputable def r (k N : ℕ) : ℕ := (Finset.Icc 1 N).maxAPFreeCard k

/--
Problem 9 (i): is $r_3(N) \ll N(\log N)^{-10}$?

Solved in [BlSi20].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem green_9_i :
    (fun (N : ℕ) ↦ (r 3 N : ℝ)) ≪ fun (N : ℕ) ↦ (N : ℝ) * (Real.log N) ^ (-10 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Problem 9 (ii): is $r_5(N) \ll N(\log N)^{-c}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem green_9_ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), (fun (N : ℕ) ↦ (r 5 N : ℝ))
      ≪ fun (N : ℕ) ↦ (N : ℝ) * (Real.log N) ^ (-c) := by
  sorry

/--
Problem 9 (iii): is $r_4(\mathbf{F}_5^n) \ll N^{1-c}$, where $N=5^n$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem green_9_iii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ ((Finset.univ : Finset (𝔽₅ n)).maxAPFreeCard 4 : ℝ))
      ≪ fun (n : ℕ) ↦ ((5 : ℝ) ^ n) ^ (1 - c) := by
  sorry

-- TODO(jeangud): Add some additional bounds from the literature.

end Green9

findings.description: The docstring says "Solved in [BlSi20]". The module docstring defines [BlSi20] as Bloom–Sisask, "Breaking the logarithmic barrier in Roth's theorem on arithmetic progressions", arXiv:2007.03528 (2020). That paper does not solve Problem 9(i). Its main theorem is only r_3(N) ≪ N/(log N)^{1+c} for some tiny absolute c > 0; the authors estimate c ≈ 2^{-2^{2^{1000}}}. This is far from N(log N)^{-10}. Part (i) was settled in 2023 by Kelley–Meka (arXiv:2302.05537), with the exponent improved to 1/9 by a later Bloom–Sisask paper (arXiv:2309.02353). Green cites these two as [194] and [39]. The Lean statement itself is correct: it is exactly the solved claim, and its `research solved` tag is right. Only the attribution, and the reference entry it points to, are wrong.
findings.source_evidence: Green, 100 open problems (PDF, version dated December 2025), Problem 9, Comments: "Update 2024. In a remarkable breakthrough, Kelley and Meka [194] have proved an upper bound of the shape r_3(N) ≪ N e^{-c(log N)^β}, and Bloom and Sisask [39] have shown that one can take β = 1/9." In Green's bibliography: [39] = "T. Bloom and O. Sisask, An improvement to the Kelley-Meka bounds on three-term arithmetic progressions, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02353"; [194] = "Z. Kelley and R. Meka, Strong bounds for 3-progressions, https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.05537". arXiv:2007.03528 abstract: "|A| ≪ N/(log N)^{1+c} for some absolute constant c>0"; Roth.tex footnote: "c ≈ 2^{-2^{2^{1000}}} should be achievable". Kelley–Meka abstract: "Previously, three-term arithmetic progressions were known to exist only for sets of size at least N/(log N)^{1+c}".
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [BlSi20] entry in the module docstring with the solving references, for example `[KeMe23] Kelley, Zander, and Raghu Meka. "Strong bounds for 3-progressions." FOCS 2023, arXiv:2302.05537` and `[BlSi23] Bloom, Thomas F., and Olof Sisask. "An improvement to the Kelley–Meka bounds on three-term arithmetic progressions." arXiv:2309.02353 (2023)`. Change the green_9_i docstring to "Solved in [KeMe23] (see also [BlSi23])." No change to the Lean statement is needed.

reformulations.difference: Green poses (i) as a yes/no question ("(Solved) Is r_3(N) ≪ N(log N)^{-10}?"). The Lean states the affirmative claim P directly, instead of the `answer(True) ↔ P` form that CONTRIBUTING prefers for solved questions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `(True ↔ P) ↔ P` holds for every proposition P. The answer is affirmative (Kelley–Meka), so asserting P is exactly `answer(True) ↔ P`. The direction of `≪` is right: `g ≪ f` unfolds to `g =O[atTop] f`, with r_3 on the left.

sources_consulted: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf (Problem 9 and its comments on pp. 6–7; section 2 intro defining r_k(N) and r_k(G); bibliography entries [39], [194], [210]; 'Most recent update: December 2025')
https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.03528 and its LaTeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/2007.03528 (Roth.tex: main theorem, and the footnote on the size of c)
https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Szemer%C3%A9di%27s_theorem&action=raw (current bounds for r_3, r_4 and r_5)
review.notes:
Checks performed (scratch files in /workspace/review):

1. **Elaboration.** I ran `#check` with `pp.explicit` on all three theorems. `≪` unfolds to `Asymptotics.IsBigO atTop` with the intended direction. All exponents are real powers (`(log N)^(-10)`, `(log N)^(-c)`, `(5^n)^(1-c)`). The `∃ c > 0` sits inside the iff, after `answer(sorry)`. `𝔽₅ n` is `Fin n → ZMod 5` with the pointwise additive structure.

2. **The definition `r` / `maxAPFreeCard`.** It counts only non-trivial progressions: `IsAPOfLengthWith` requires `encard = k`, so d = 0 is excluded. In F_5^n a 4-term progression with d ≠ 0 always has four distinct points. I proved two small cases in Lean:
   - `r 3 3 = 2`, which matches OEIS A003002;
   - `3 ≤ r₄(𝔽₅ 1) ≤ 4` (the whole of F_5 contains the 4-term progression {0,1,2,3}).

3. **Boundary values.** `N·(log N)^{-c}` evaluates to 0 at N = 0 and N = 1, but this does not matter under `atTop`. `(5^n)^{1-c}` is positive for every n, so eventual big-O is the same as a uniform bound with an absolute constant.

4. **(ii) and (iii).** Both use `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, …`, in the same direction as Green's questions, so neither is a negated conjecture. The `research open` tags match the source. Green's December 2025 version records only the 2024 Leng–Sah–Sawhney bound `r_k(N) ≪ N·exp(-(log log N)^{c_k})` for k ≥ 5, which is \"not as strong as (ii)\". For (iii) it says \"this has not been achieved at present\". Wikipedia's current bounds agree.

5. **Blocked lookups.** The arXiv API refused my queries (HTTP 429) and erdosproblems.com is behind a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403). So I could not search for anything newer than Green's December 2025 update, and I don't list those sites as sources.
